title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 413, page 1-38), photographed upside down. The page was evidently reused as scrap paper for the handwritten notes on motives found on the neighbouring pages (the canonical extension 0→G^0→G→Γ, fibre functors at places ξ, Hodge structures).

The content belongs to the theory of point distributions (distributions ponctuelles) on a Lie group, or more generally an analytic or C^r group manifold. This material became Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, Ch. III, §3. In modern terms:
- 𝒯^{(r)}(G) is the space of point distributions of order ≤ r on G.
- Convolution t*t' is the pushforward of t⊗t' under multiplication. It is defined when the orders satisfy s+s' ≤ r.

Example 1: Inversion Θ: x↦x^{-1} is an isomorphism from G onto the opposite group G^0. It therefore gives an anti-involution on distributions: (t*t')^∨ = ť' * ť.

Example 2:
- For a subgroup manifold H ⊂ G, 𝒯^{(r)}(H) embeds in 𝒯^{(r)}(G) compatibly with convolution.
- If H_1 and H_2 commute elementwise, distributions supported on them commute. Both t_1*t_2 and t_2*t_1 are images of t_1⊗t_2 under (h_1,h_2)↦h_1h_2 = h_2h_1.
- Hence 𝒯^{(r)}(G) is commutative when G is commutative.

For r = ∞ (or ω), convolution makes 𝒯^{(r)}(G) an associative algebra. Here φ_* is an algebra homomorphism for every C^∞ group morphism φ. In particular, 𝒯(G^0) is the opposite algebra of 𝒯(G).

The subspace T_e^{(r)}(G) of distributions supported at the identity is stable under the partially defined convolution. It is denoted U(G); for r ≥ ∞ it is an associative algebra, to be identified in §3 with the universal enveloping algebra of Lie(G). This is the standard distribution-algebra description of U(𝔤).
errors: Minor grammatical slip in the typescript: 'deux sous-variétés de groupe de G tels que' should read 'telles que'.
No mathematical errors. The identity (23) and the commutativity argument are correct, given the usual order constraints s+s' ≤ r.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine Bourbaki draft on point distributions, reused as scrap paper beneath Grothendieck's motivic notes. Its content is standard and was published in Bourbaki Lie III. The only point of mild archival interest is that it shows Grothendieck reusing Bourbaki drafts (n° 413) for his notes around 1965.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (n° 413), not Grothendieck's handwriting.

The typescript distinguishes the space 𝒯^{(r)}(G) (script T) from T^{(r)}(G) and T_e^{(r)}(G) (roman T). The transcription mixes these somewhat inconsistently, e.g. 't ∈ T^{(r)}(G)' and 't_i ∈ T^{(s_i)}(H_i)'.
'r ≥ ∞' is as typed: Bourbaki's convention allows r ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞, ω}.
The archive's handwritten page number '161' appears at the bottom left of the upside-down image.
